body: Hello! May I ask if the issue is still reproducible in Godot 4.5 (stable)?

@Nintorch Yes, still present. I reproduced it on current `master` (4.8.dev, b56a918) on macOS with an OpenTX RadioMaster Pocket in USB joystick mode, so it isn't Linux- or evdev-specific. `drivers/sdl/joypad_sdl.cpp` in 4.5, 4.6 an>

With an untouched transmitter, every axis reads `0.000` for as long as you care to wait:

```
[frame 1] device 0 axes [0:+0.000 1:+0.000 2:+0.000 3:+0.000 4:+0.000 5:+0.000 6:+0.000 7:+0.000]
```

I think the cause is a bit different from the description in the OP, though. It isn't that the initial state can't be queried — SDL has it, on both platforms:

- Linux: `PollAllValues()` in `joystick/linux/SDL_sysjoystick.c` reads every axis with an `EVIOCGABS` ioctl and feeds the results to `SDL_SendJoystickAxis()`.
- macOS: `DARWIN_JoystickUpdate()` in `joystick/darwin/SDL_iokitjoystick.c` polls each axis element via `IOHIDDeviceGetValue()` on every update.

The value reaches SDL without anyone touching the device. What stops it reaching Godot is that SDL deliberately withholds the *event*, in `SDL_SendJoystickAxis()`:

```c
if (!info->sent_initial_value) {
    // Make sure we don't send motion until there's real activity on this axis
    const int MAX_ALLOWED_JITTER = SDL_JOYSTICK_AXIS_MAX / 80;
    if (SDL_abs(value - info->value) <= MAX_ALLOWED_JITTER && ...) {
        return;
    }
    ...
}
```

The first value SDL sees becomes that axis' baseline, and no motion event is emitted until the axis moves ~2.5% away from it. Since the driver only ever updates from those events, Godot keeps reporting the default `0.0` for any con>

SDL exposes what's needed to fix this at the driver level, without patching vendored SDL: `SDL_GetJoystickAxisInitialState()` reports whether SDL has an initial value for an axis, and `SDL_GetJoystickAxis()` returns the current one.

I've opened a draft PR for this: #122817. It's a two-file change to the SDL driver for raw joysticks, with no new scripting API. Same device, same conditions, untouched:

```
[frame 1] device 0 axes [0:+0.006 1:+0.005 2:-1.000 3:+0.002 4:-1.000 5:+1.000 6:-1.000 7:-1.000]
```

Axis 2 is the throttle at minimum, 4-7 are switches (this device reports them as axes), 0/1/3 are the gimbals' real resting offsets. Moving the throttle to about quarter travel and reconnecting gives `2:-0.242` on frame 1, so it re>
